mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the expected S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to tightened financing conditions affecting corporate investment and consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) when the trigger occurs, or the FEDFUNDS increase is <0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for more than three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as expectations of future disinflation boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative or flat despite three consecutive monthly CPI drops of >0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs coincides with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as labor market strength supports corporate optimism and equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: Over 20 consecutive months of PAYEMS > 200,000, the 20-day forward return remains negative or shows no statistically significant correlation (R² < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls by double-digits in a month, the S&P 60-day forward return turns negative as weak manufacturing demand reduces economic momentum and equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >10% in a month
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive despite INDPRO falling >10% in the trigger month, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in RSAFS of at least 15% predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as tight supply conditions drive up relative demand for equities as alternative assets.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases for 2 consecutive months by >15% each
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05) when the trigger is met, or the decline in RSAFS is not consecutive or <15%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5% for three consecutive months, the S&P 60-day forward return turns positive as labor market tightness supports economic expansion and equity valuations.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative or flat despite three consecutive months of UNRATE below 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent FEDFUNDS above 5%, the S&P 5-day forward return is consistently negative due to the immediate impact of higher short-term rates on risk-free discounting of equity cash flows.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month period of FEDFUNDS > 5%, the 5-day forward return is not negative or shows no correlation (R² < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in consumer demand measured by HOUST exceeding 2,000 units in a month coincides with a positive 20-day S&P forward return as the surge accelerates inventory turnover and supports production capacity expansion.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >500 units in a month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not positive or statistically significant (p > 0.05) when the trigger is met, or the increase in HOUST is not >500 units.
